articles.title: Médico preso na Paraíba: suspeita de assédio em UBS de Caaporã | G1
articles.standfirst: Segundo a Polícia Civil, o caso foi registrado em uma UBS na zona rural de Caaporã, no Litoral Sul da Paraíba.
articles.summary: O médico preso na Paraíba é investigado por atos libidinosos em uma UBS de Caaporã após denúncias de pacientes de 20 e 44 anos; ele nega as acusações à polícia.
articles.body:
Delegacia de Alhandra, no Litoral Sul da Paraíba — Foto: Antônio Vieira

Um médico foi preso em flagrante, na tarde desta quarta-feira (4), suspeito de praticar atos libidinosos contra pacientes durante atendimentos. Segundo a Polícia Civil, o caso foi registrado em Caaporã , no Litoral Sul da Paraíba.

O médico, que não teve a sua identificação divulgada, atendia em uma Unidade Básica de Saúde (UBS) na zona rural do município. As investigações tiveram início após uma paciente de 20 anos procurar a delegacia e denunciar que teria sido vítima de conduta sexual inadequada durante uma consulta realizada na manhã desta quarta-feira.

Segundo o relato, o médico teria utilizado a justificativa de procedimentos clínicos para realizar toques e manipulações íntimas sem finalidade médica, além de fazer questionamentos de cunho sexual durante o atendimento.

Após a denúncia, equipes da Polícia Civil iniciaram diligências na unidade de saúde e identificaram outros relatos envolvendo a conduta do profissional. Uma segunda paciente, de 44 anos, também procurou a polícia e relatou ter sido submetida a situações semelhantes durante atendimento anterior no mesmo estabelecimento.

Funcionários da unidade também foram ouvidos e relataram comportamentos inadequados e situações de constrangimento atribuídas ao suspeito. Assim, o médico foi preso em flagrante e deve passar por audiência de custódia. Em depoimento, ele alegou que os contatos tiveram finalidade exclusivamente diagnóstica e assistencial.

Para subsidiar as investigações, foram requisitados exames periciais ao Instituto de Polícia Científica (IPC), por meio do Núcleo de Medicina e Odontologia Legal (NUMOL), além de solicitadas as imagens do sistema de monitoramento interno da unidade de saúde.

articles.title: Acidente na MGC-491 em Varginha deixa uma mulher morta e um ferido | G1
articles.standfirst: Acidente envolvendo dois veículos ocorreu na noite desta quarta-feira (4), próximo ao trevo da AABB; vítima de 77 anos foi levada ao Hospital Bom Pastor.
articles.summary: O acidente na MGC-491 em Varginha ocorreu na noite de quarta-feira perto do trevo da AABB; o sobrevivente de 77 anos foi levado ao Hospital Bom Pastor.
articles.body:
Mulher morre e idoso fica ferido em capotamento na MGC-491, em Varginha — Foto: Corpo de Bombeiros

Uma mulher de 39 anos morreu e um homem de 77 anos ficou ferido após um capotamento envolvendo dois veículos na Rodovia MGC-491, nas proximidades do trevo da AABB, em Varginha . O acidente aconteceu na noite desta quarta-feira (4), por volta das 18h15.

Segundo o Corpo de Bombeiros Militar e o Serviço de Atendimento Móvel de Urgência (SAMU), o homem sofreu lesões leves e estava consciente e orientado durante o atendimento. Ele foi imobilizado e encaminhado pelo SAMU ao Hospital Bom Pastor para avaliação médica.

A outra vítima, uma mulher de 39 anos, não resistiu à gravidade dos ferimentos e morreu ainda no local do acidente.

A Polícia Militar e a Polícia Civil foram acionadas para o registro da ocorrência, isolamento da área e realização da perícia técnica.

As circunstâncias e as possíveis causas do acidente serão apuradas pelas autoridades.

articles.title: Telangana bus conductor dies 10 days after woman passenger pushes her off moving bus
articles.summary: TGSRTC conductor Gundla Pravalika dies 10 days after being pushed off a moving bus in Bhadradri-Kothagudem; passenger B Mounika booked for murder.
articles.body: HYDERABAD: Ten days after she was allegedly pushed off a moving bus by a woman passenger, Gundla Pravalika, a conductor with the Telangana State Road Transport Corporation (TGSRTC), succumbed to her injuries at a private hospital in Hyderabad on Wednesday.She had sustained grievous injuries in the incident at Mittagudem Centre in Aswapuram mandal of Bhadradri-Kothagudem district.Following Pravalika’s death, Aswapuram police altered the case against the accused, B Mounika, from attempt to murder to murder.“The accused, who was arrested earlier, continues to be in judicial remand,” Ch Yallaiah, station house officer of Aswapuram police station, told TOI. “Although the conductor received treatment, she died due to blood loss. The victim was unmarried,” he added.The incident occurred on October 25, when Pravalika was on duty, operating a bus between Manuguru and Bhadrachalam along with driver K Jampaiah.Woman picked fight over 10, say policeA heated argument reportedly broke out between Pravalika and Mounika over change for the bus fare. During the altercation, Mounika allegedly pushed the conductor out of the moving bus, causing her right leg to come under the rear wheels.The 24-year-old conductor was rushed to a local hospital, where she received initial treatment. She was subsequently shifted to a private hospital in Hyderabad for further treatment, but succumbed to her injuries.Chief minister A Revanth Reddy expressed grief over Pravalika’s death and conveyed his condolences to her family. “He conveyed deep condolences and sympathy to her family members.The CM stated that the state govt will stand by Pravalika’s family and provide help,” the Chief Minister’s Office said in a post on X.Following the CM’s instructions, the state govt announced a job for Pravalika’s mother, a house for the family under the Indiramma Housing Scheme and an ex gratia of Rs 10 lakh. The family will also be provided insurance cover of Rs 1 crore, transport minister Ponnam Prabhakar said.The minister visited Osmania General Hospital, where Pravalika’s postmortem examination was conducted.According to police, Mounika boarded the bus around 9am on the day of the incident at the Manuguru flower market, accompanied by her son. She availed herself of a zero-fare ticket by furnishing her Aadhaar card and handed Pravalika a Rs 100 note to purchase a half ticket, priced at Rs 10, for her minor son.“When the female conductor asked for Rs 10 in change, the accused refused. This led to an argument, and the accused allegedly hurled abuses at the victim,” a police officer said.The bus was subsequently stopped, and Mounika was asked to get down. However, she refused and insisted that the RTC staff drop her at the point where she had boarded the bus, police said.As the driver resumed the journey, the argument reportedly continued. When the bus reached Mittagudem Centre, Mounika allegedly pushed Pravalika out of the moving vehicle, causing her serious injuries.Mounika had claimed that the conductor was standing on the footboard and had accidentally fallen off the bus. articles.title: Lions teammates encouraged by latest update on Jack Campbell
articles.summary: Detroit Lions linebacker Jack Campbell says he has full lower body movement while recovering from a neck injury, giving his teams a sense of relief.
articles.body:
ALLEN PARK — Derrick Barnes remains eager to have his own conversation with Jack Campbell, but the latest update regarding his fellow linebacker has Barnes and his Detroit Lions teammates feeling a sense of relief.

Campbell, who was carted off the field with a neck injury against the Minnesota Vikings on Sunday, Nov. 1, said in a statement through the team Wednesday he has "full movement in my lower body , and I'm continuing to make progress with movement in my upper body. I know there's still work ahead, but I remain very optimistic."

"I love to see his progression," Barnes said Wednesday. "Jack is a strong guy, a strong man, a man of God. I know he's putting a lot of faith into God right now, like he always is. It really gave me a boost of energy to hear that. Like I said, he's one of the strongest people I know. If anybody can get through this, it'd definitely be him."

Campbell went limp after he made what appeared to be a routine tackle against Vikings tight end T.J. Hockenson early in the fourth quarter of Sunday's win . His teammates knelt around him while the team's medical staff stabilized his neck and placed him on a backboard. He was transported to Henry Ford Hospital.

Barnes tried to visit Campbell at the hospital Sunday but was unable to do so. Lions coach Dan Campbell said Wednesday, "Everybody wants to see Jack. Unfortunately, it doesn't work that way, just with where it's at."

The Lions met as a team Wednesday morning and discussed Campbell's situation. Quarterback Jared Goff acknowledged "it's been hard," but "Dan hit it right on the head" with his message as the Lions prepare to play the Miami Dolphins at Hard Rock Stadium on Sunday, Nov. 8.

"It's obviously so much bigger than just football," Goff said. "I think you're happy that things are moving in the right direction, but yeah, there's still certainly some emotion attached to it, how scary it was and whatnot.

"I think the best thing we can do is play how he would want us to play and kind of honor him in that way. I know he doesn't he want any attention, he doesn't want any fanfare. He just wants us to go out there and handle our business, and that's what we plan to do."

Asked how he felt when he was told the latest on Campbell, Malcolm Rodriguez described it as a "sigh of relief." Barnes and Rodriguez cried with each other in the locker room at Ford Field after Sunday's contest, once their adrenaline from the game wore off and the gravity of Campbell's injury fully hit them.

"It's a lot that goes through your mind," Rodriguez said. "At the moment, you're like, 'Jack, get up, get up.' Thinking about his family, Megan (Campbell's wife) and Coop (Campbell's four-month-old son). I just put myself in that position, what they're going through. ... It definitely hit us after the game. I spent my night hugging my family."

Barnes added: "That really hit me because it's like, man, no way that happened to someone like that, a man who is selfless. He is like the most selfless person ever. He puts everybody before himself all the time, makes sure everybody is good before himself. For something like that to happen to somebody like that, it's really devastating. ... It hits harder when it's somebody like him."

A teammate of Campbell's for the last four seasons, Barnes said seeing him get hurt has been the hardest challenge of his career. A number of Lions have said the sobering situation put things into perspective. Barnes went home after the game and told his two-year-old son, Trey, he'd rather him not play football when he gets older.

"We can have a long conversation," Barnes said of the eventual talk he'll have with Trey. "I'll tell you the great things about it and the down things about it, and you'll make that decision if you really want to."

An official diagnosis for Campbell or a timeline for his recovery has not yet been shared publicly. In his statement, Campbell asked for fans to "continue to keep me and my family in your prayers. We feel the love, and I can't thank everyone enough."

"When you spend almost every day of the year with a guy, around him literally every day, it hits different. ... When you become very close with a person (and) anything like this happens, obviously you're concerned and you're worried," Barnes said. "But you know deep down in your heart, put your faith into God and know that God has it. I truly believe that he'll get back to where he started."

articles.title: O que se sabe sobre a morte de Janaína Barbosa, ex-apresentadora que sofreu choque anafilático por medicação | G1
articles.standfirst: Jornalista e psicanalista morreu aos 48 anos, em São Paulo; artista trocou medicação e teve reação alérgica grave.
articles.summary: Jornalista e psicanalista morreu aos 48 anos, em São Paulo; artista trocou medicação e teve reação alérgica grave.
articles.body:
A morte foi confirmada ao g1 pelo apresentador Otávio Mesquita , ex-marido de Janaína, e por Camila Avesani , amiga da artista. Camila disse não saber informar o nome do remédio que Janaína ingeriu e afirmou estar devastada com a perda. "Estou sem rumo", declarou.

Otávio também lamentou a morte da ex-mulher. "Ainda não sei como isso aconteceu, mas mandei recado para a mãe dela. Ela [Janaína] era uma pessoa muito correta, fomos casados há 20 anos. Tenho respeito por ela", afirmou ao g1 .

O velório aconteceu na tarde da última quarta-feira (4), em São Paulo, e foi restrito a familiares e amigos próximos.

A morte também provocou manifestações de pesar entre amigos e pessoas próximas. Marina Mantega , filha do ex-ministro Guido Mantega, lamentou a perda em uma publicação nas redes sociais.

"Sem palavras para descrever o que eu estou sentindo. Literalmente sem chão. Ainda sem acreditar em tudo isso... Te amo muito! Você fará falta, muita falta em nossas vidas", escreveu.

Janaína ganhou projeção na televisão no início dos anos 2000 , quando apresentou o programa "TV Fama", da RedeTV!, ao lado de Nelson Rubens.

Além do trabalho como apresentadora, também investiu na carreira de atriz e participou da série "Casos e Acasos", exibida pela TV Globo em 2008.

Ao longo da trajetória artística, trabalhou como bailarina e produtora de teatro. Em 2007, foi madrinha de bateria da escola de samba Mocidade Independente de Padre Miguel, no Carnaval do Rio de Janeiro.

A causa da morte de Janaína Barbosa foi choque anafilático, em decorrência de uma reação alérgica extrema a uma medicação nova.

A reação pode acontecer rapidamente e provocar sintomas como dificuldade para respirar, inchaço na garganta, queda brusca da pressão arterial e alterações nos batimentos cardíacos.

Em casos mais graves, pode levar à perda de consciência e até à morte. É uma emergência médica que exige atendimento imediato.

Janaína Barbosa sofreu o choque após trocar uma medição e ter reação alérgica.

Não se sabe qual remédio provocou a reação alérgica em Janaína Barbosa.

Camila Avesani, amiga próxima de Janaína Barbosa, foi quem confirmou a causa da morte da ex-apresentadora por choque anafilático. Sem dar detalhes, a comunicadora disse que não sabe qual medicação causou a reação adversa.

Otávio Mesquita, ex-marido de Janaína, soube de seu falecimento, mas não foi informado sobre a causa.

6. O que Janaína fazia nos últimos anos?

Nos últimos anos, Janaína Barbosa de Siqueira estava longe dos holofotes e passou a se dedicar à psicologia.

Formada em psicologia e jornalismo, atuava como psicanalista e atendia em consultório. Também era colaboradora do Laboratório de Pesquisa Sujeito e Corpo (SuCor), do Instituto de Psicologia da USP, vinculado ao Grupo de Pesquisa CNPq: Grupo Interdisciplinar de Estudos e Pesquisas em Psicossomática.

Tinha experiência em Psicologia Clínica, Psicologia da Saúde, Psicologia Hospitalar e Psicossomática. Também atuava como psicóloga hospitalar colaboradora do Hospital Universitário da USP.

Janaína também teve um relacionamento com o apresentador Otávio Mesquita. Os dois começaram a namorar em 2001 e oficializaram a união no ano seguinte.

Em 2006, chegaram a se separar, mas reataram o relacionamento em dezembro do mesmo ano. O casamento terminou oficialmente em 2007.

Em 2010, Janaína se casou novamente, desta vez com o empresário Felipe Faria, neto de Aloysio de Andrade Faria, fundador do Banco Alfa.

A cerimônia aconteceu à beira-mar, na Ilha de Comandatuba, na Bahia. Os dois tiveram dois filhos, Bernardo e Frederico. Atualmente, ambos estavam separados.

Ainda não há abertura de inquérito para apurar a morte.

articles.title: Polícia investiga se houve falha humana em queda de asa-delta  | G1
articles.standfirst: Polícia também investiga se houve falha humana em outro caso com duas mortes em fevereiro deste ano. Advogado avalia que pode não haver responsabilização criminal.
articles.summary: Polícia também investiga se houve falha humana em outro caso com duas mortes em fevereiro deste ano. Advogado avalia que deve haver responsabilização criminal.
articles.body:
A Polícia Civil investiga se as mortes do instrutor de voo livre Luiz Eduardo Rodrigues dos Santos e do passageiro argentino Adrian Guillermo Arismendi, de 26 anos, na manhã de segunda-feira (2), foram causadas por um erro do próprio instrutor durante uma manobra de asa-delta.

Peritos da Polícia Civil estiveram no Clube São Conrado de Voo Livre para analisar o equipamento, que fazia apenas seu terceiro voo. O clube deve enviar para a 15ª DP (Gávea) até sexta-feira (6) um documento de análise do acidente.

O g1 apurou que há pelo menos um outro caso com características semelhantes, segundo a delegacia. Em fevereiro de 2026 , o instrutor de voo livre Rodolfo Pascoal Ladeira, piloto e instrutor, e a turista colombiana naturalizada americana Jenny Colôn Rodríguez morreram quando a asa-delta onde estavam caiu no mar da praia de São Conrado.

Rodolfo chegou sem vida à areia . Jenny foi socorrida em estado grave e encaminhada ao Hospital Municipal Miguel Couto, na Gávea, mas não resistiu.

Um relatório de análise do acidente de fevereiro, feito pelo Clube São Conrado de Voo Livre e obtido pelo g1, atestou que não havia danos prévios ao equipamento e que as condições meteorológicas eram propícias para a atividade de voo livre.

"Não se pôde determinar de maneira conclusiva o que de fato ocasionou o acidente, ficando em aberto a conclusão final desta análise (falha estrutural, imperícia etc)", diz o trecho final do relatório.

Em entrevista ao RJ2 após o acidente que terminou com a morte de Adrian e Luiz Eduardo, o vice-presidente do Clube São Conrado de Voo Livre, José Bruno Batalha Menescal Filho, afirmou que a única explicação para tantos acidentes fatais é o fator humano:

"Eu acho que o ser humano. Simplesmente a atividade e o ser humano. É isso que nós vamos rever. Não tem explicação, com todo rigor que a gente tem: não tem explicação", disse ele.

Em caso de falha humana causando a morte dos passageiros e dos próprios instrutores, o advogado criminalista Breno Melaragno avalia que esse cenário pode resultar em uma extinção de punibilidade.

"Em direito penal, a conduta é sempre individual. O que é extinção da punibilidade? É quando não há mais possibilidade da pessoa ser punida por eventual crime, a primeira causa delas é a morte", explicou o advogado.

"O que se destina a investigação é descobrir se mais alguém teve culpa no acidente, além do instrutor", pontuou.

Em 2026, a média de ocorrências com asa-delta e parapente na cidade do Rio é de um acidente a cada 19 dias. Foram 16 acionamentos do Corpo de Bombeiros para atender vítimas que praticavam voo livre.

Em 2025, foram 20 acionamentos. Em 2024, foram 15 vezes que os bombeiros foram acionados.

Instrutor responde por homicídio culposo

O instrutor de voo Sérgio Manoel da Silva responde na Justiça do Rio pelo homicídio culposo (quando não há intenção de matar) do piloto americano Phil Haegler após um acidente em novembro de 2025 em São Conrado, na Zona Sul do Rio.

A denúncia do Ministério Público do Rio contra Sergio foi aceita pela 16ª Vara Criminal no dia 16 de outubro. Ele responde em liberdade.

O caso de Phil Haegler foi um dos acidentes que terminaram em morte na região desde o ano passado.

De acordo com o presidente do Clube São Conrado de Voo Live, Bruno Menescal, Sergio não pode atuar como instrutor:

"Afastado por tempo indeterminado, sujeito a avaliação psicológica", respondeu Menescal ao g1.

O relatório final da 15ª DP (Gávea) apontou que Sergio agiu com "negligência" e "desatenção" , não observando as regras de segurança do voo desportivo.

O piloto disse que voava com um aluno e se distraiu por instantes ao se aproximar do pouso, causando o acidente. Segundo Sergio Manoel, Phil não cometeu erro algum. O instrutor admitiu à polícia que errou.

O piloto afirmou que, ao se aproximar da área de pouso, olhou para baixo para soltar a perneira do aluno, uma manobra padrão, e perdeu a visão do parapente de Haegler por "cerca de três segundos".

Ao olhar novamente para frente, Sergio Manoel disse que se assustou ao ver o parapente conduzido por Haegler e tentou fazer um movimento brusco, mas não conseguiu evitar a colisão.

Ele afirmou ainda que a barra da asa-delta e seu corpo encostaram no parapente, e que ficou desesperado ao perceber que Haegler não conseguiu recuperar o voo.

O g1 não conseguiu contato com a defesa de Sergio Manoel da Silva.

articles.title: Hospital Souza Aguiar: Homem é preso após quebrar vidro e ferir dois | G1
articles.standfirst: Imagens de câmeras de segurança mostram o momento em que o homem dá um soco no vidro, que se estilhaça. Em seguida, ele deixa o local.
articles.summary: Após quebrar o vidro da radiologia do Hospital Souza Aguiar com um soco e ferir dois funcionários, Cláudio Douglas Ribeiro da Silva foi preso por policiais civis.
articles.body:
Um homem foi preso após quebrar o vidro da recepção do setor de Radiologia do Hospital Municipal Souza Aguiar, no Centro do Rio, e ferir dois funcionários. O caso aconteceu na manhã de quarta-feira (4).

Imagens de câmeras de segurança mostram o momento em que o homem dá um soco no vidro, que se estilhaça. Em seguida, ele deixa o local.

Policiais civis que estavam no hospital acompanhando presos que aguardavam atendimento médico presenciaram a cena e renderam o homem, identificado como Cláudio Douglas Ribeiro da Silva.

Ele foi levado para a delegacia e vai responder por dano qualificado contra o patrimônio público e lesão corporal.

Homem é preso após quebrar vidro da recepção do Souza Aguiar — Foto: Reprodução/TV Globo

Segundo a direção do Hospital Souza Aguiar, os dois funcionários foram atingidos por estilhaços, receberam atendimento médico e passam bem.

Em nota, a direção repudiou o episódio e afirmou que atos de violência em unidades de saúde colocam em risco profissionais e pacientes.

A reportagem não conseguiu contato com a defesa do preso.

articles.title: Médica Geysa Leal Corrêa vira ré e é proibida de atuar após morte | G1
articles.standfirst: Segundo o Ministério Público, intestino de paciente foi perfurado em três pontos durante cirurgia em São Gonçalo, provocando uma infecção grave. Justiça suspendeu o exercício da medicina pela acusada.
articles.summary: A médica Geysa Leal Corrêa virou ré por homicídio qualificado e foi proibida de atuar após a morte de uma paciente que teve o intestino perfurado durante uma lipoescultura.
articles.body:
A médica Geysa Leal Corrêa se tornou ré na Justiça pela morte de Aline Heloisa Lima Santos de Oliveira, ocorrida após uma lipoescultura realizada em São Gonçalo, na Região Metropolitana do Rio. O caso aconteceu em 2023.

A Justiça aceitou a denúncia do Ministério Público e determinou que a médica fique proibida de exercer a medicina. Segundo o Conselho Regional de Medicina, ela possui registro ativo no Cremerj.

Segundo a acusação, Geysa Leal Corrêa perfurou o intestino de Aline Heloisa Lima Santos de Oliveira em três pontos durante o procedimento, realizado em 13 de novembro de 2023, no Centro Médico Icaraí.

De acordo com a denúncia, as perfurações provocaram o vazamento de conteúdo fecal para a cavidade abdominal, causando peritonite fecal. O quadro evoluiu para choque séptico abdominal e a morte da paciente.

O Ministério Público sustenta que a médica "assumiu o risco de produzir o resultado letal". A acusação é de homicídio qualificado.

Segundo os promotores, o crime teria sido cometido por duas circunstâncias qualificadoras: motivo torpe, atribuído pela acusação à "ganância" , e emprego de meio cruel, devido ao sofrimento físico da paciente e à falta de uma intervenção imediata.

A denúncia afirma ainda que Aline Heloisa Lima Santos de Oliveira apresentou dores intensas e falta de ar logo após a lipoescultura, mas que os sintomas teriam sido minimizados pela médica.

Somente no dia seguinte, com a piora do quadro, a paciente foi transferida para um hospital e passou por uma cirurgia de emergência. Ela morreu nove dias depois da lipoescultura.

Para o Ministério Público, o local escolhido para a realização do procedimento também não tinha recursos adequados para atender complicações cirúrgicas graves.

Na decisão que recebeu a denúncia, a Justiça também determinou que as condições do Centro Médico Icaraí sejam fiscalizadas. Entre os itens que deverão ser checados estão alvarás, condições de higiene e a existência de centro cirúrgico e Unidade de Terapia Intensiva (UTI).

"A médica realizou os procedimento numa clínica que não tinha os equipamentos necessários pra uma caso de intercorrência grave, como é o caso dessa investigação", afirmou o promotor Antonio Carlos Fonte Pessanha.

"Ela agora vai responder por homicídio qualificado com dolo eventual. A pena agora é de 12 a 30 anos. O processo seguindo, ela vai ser submetida a júri popular, podendo ser condenada pelo corpo de jurados de São Gonçalo", finalizou o promotor.

Edson de Oliveira Júnior, marido de Aline Heloisa Lima Santos de Oliveira, afirmou à polícia que a médica e o marido dela tentaram convencê-lo a não prosseguir com a denúncia.

Em áudio enviado ao RJ1, Edson de Oliveira Júnior afirmou que recebeu uma oferta de emprego.

"Seu suposto esposo, a qual não tive contato com ele pessoalmente, só por telefone, ofereceu emprego, entendeu? Porque nessa época eu fiquei desempregado e tive que me mobilizar pra poder sustentar a minha filha e os restante das despesas", relatou.

Ao analisar o depoimento, a Justiça considerou haver indícios de coação e proibiu Geysa Leal Corrêa de manter contato com o viúvo, pessoal ou virtualmente.

Geysa Leal se tornou ré por morte de paciente durante procedimento estético — Foto: Reprodução

A denúncia afirma ainda que, quando operou Aline Heloisa Lima Santos de Oliveira, Geysa Leal Corrêa não tinha título de especialista em cirurgia plástica registrado no Cremerj.

O histórico da médica já havia sido mostrado pelo g1 em 2023. À época, ela tinha cadastro ativo no Cremerj e especializações registradas em medicina do trabalho, medicina estética e medicina ortomolecular, mas não em cirurgia plástica. A Sociedade Brasileira de Cirurgia Plástica também informou naquele momento que ela não integrava os quadros da entidade.

Na mesma época, o g1 mostrou que a médica respondia a pelo menos nove processos relacionados a alegações de erros médicos no Tribunal de Justiça do Rio: sete ações cíveis e duas na esfera criminal.

A atual denúncia cita as mortes de outras duas pacientes que passaram por procedimentos realizados pela médica: Adriana Ferreira Capitão Pinto, em 2018, e Silvia de Oliveira Martins, em setembro de 2023, dois meses antes da cirurgia de Aline.

Adriana Ferreira Capitão Pinto morreu seis dias depois de uma cirurgia realizada em 2018. Geysa Leal Corrêa foi condenada em primeira instância, em 2022, por homicídio culposo com inobservância de regra técnica da profissão. Questionado sobre a condenação, o Cremerj não respondeu.

Adriana Ferreira Capitão Pinto era moradora de Paracambi, no Sul do Rio — Foto: Foto/Divulgação

Já Silvia era advogada do MC Marlon Brendon Coelho, o MC Poze, e morreu em 2023 após fazer uma lipoaspiração.

"A declaração de óbito dela diz que morreu por choque hemorrágico por tromboembolismo pulmonar, em razão de lipoaspiração recente", disse o então advogado de Silvia ao g1 em 2023.

Silvia de Oliveira Martins: ela se submeteu a uma lipo HD — Foto: Reprodução/Redes sociais

Mesmo após os episódios anteriores, Geysa Leal Corrêa continuava divulgando procedimentos estéticos nas redes sociais até o mês passado. Em uma das publicações, a médica aparece falando sobre uma harmonização facial com enxerto de gordura.

Em nota, o Cremerj afirmou que a profissional está regular no Conselho e que, até o momento, não foi recebida nenhuma notificação judicial a respeito do caso. O Cremerj reitera que, ao receber, "cumprirá qualquer ordem judicial".

O RJ1 entrou em contato com a médica Geysa e o Centro Médico Icaraí, mas não teve retorno até a publicação desta reportagem.

articles.title: Jovem que sumiu após cair em golpe é encontrado morto no litoral de SP | G1
articles.standfirst: O corpo foi encontrado em avançado estado de decomposição em uma área de mata em Guarujá (SP). A informação foi confirmada pela advogada Bianca Santiago, que representa amigos e familiares do jovem.
articles.summary: Corpo foi encontrado em estado avançado de decomposição em uma área de mata em Guarujá (SP) e foi reconhecido como José Luis da Costa Oliveira apenas após passar por exames.
articles.body:
José Luis da Costa Oliveira, o analista de sistemas de 25 anos que desapareceu após cair em um golpe durante a venda do próprio carro , foi encontrado morto em Guarujá , no litoral de São Paulo. O corpo, em avançado estado de decomposição, passou por exames para a confirmação da identidade, segundo a advogada Bianca Santiago, que representa amigos e familiares do jovem.

Natural do Pará (PA), José se mudou para a capital paulista a trabalho e desapareceu no dia 8 de outubro , após cair em um golpe durante a venda do próprio carro e viajar para o litoral de São Paulo. Antes da viagem, o analista de sistemas gravou um vídeo relatando a fraude ( assista acima ).

A gravação foi encontrada cerca de três dias depois do desaparecimento, no computador de José, que estava desbloqueado no apartamento dele, no bairro Bela Vista, na capital .

No vídeo, o jovem afirmou que os compradores do carro não tinham envolvimento com o golpe, que teria sido cometido pelo intermediador da venda (entenda mais abaixo) .

José Luis foi encontrado morto em Guarujá — Foto: Reprodução/Redes sociais e Arquivo Pessoal

O corpo do homem foi encontrado no dia 22 de outubro , após moradores acionarem a Polícia Militar (PM) se queixando de um forte odor na Avenida General Rondon, no bairro Vila Alzira, em Guarujá.

O Corpo de Bombeiros foi acionado e três agentes encontraram o corpo em área de mata. O avançado estado de decomposição do cadáver não permitiu o reconhecimento. A vítima só foi confirmada após exames ao Instituto de Criminalística e ao Instituto Médico Legal.

José Luis da Costa Oliveira foi até um bar no bairro Boqueirão, em Santos. — Foto: Arquivo Pessoal e Reprodução

A identificação de José foi confirmada pela advogada Bianca Santiago, que representa os amigos e familiares do jovem, em nota publicada nas redes sociais, na quarta-feira (4).

“É com profundo pesar que informamos que o corpo localizado em Guarujá/SP foi identificado como sendo de José Luís da Costa Oliveira”, afirmava o comunicado.

Segundo o texto, não foi possível determinar a causa da morte devido ao estado avançado de decomposição. “Pela forma como o corpo foi localizado, há indícios de suicídio, mas a investigação continua, e seguiremos acompanhando o caso até a sua conclusão”, disse.

Ainda segundo a advogada, o corpo deverá ser levado ao estado do Pará e, portanto, não há informações sobre o velório.

“Sentimos muito pela perda. Que a família e os amigos de José encontrem conforto e força neste momento”.

Procurada pelo g1 , a Secretaria de Segurança Pública de São Paulo (SSP-SP) não se manifestou sobre o caso.

José Luis da Costa Oliveira, de 25 anos, gravou vídeo chorando — Foto: Reprodução

O golpista, que não teve o nome divulgado, entrou em contato com José após o analista de sistemas anunciar a venda do carro nas redes sociais. Ele se ofereceu para intermediar a negociação e o jovem aceitou a proposta.

Uma compradora se interessou e tratou sobre a venda com o suspeito. Sendo assim, José transferiu o carro para a mulher. Ela depositou o valor da compra na conta do intermediador, que sumiu.

“A pessoa que comprou o carro depositou o valor de R$ 24 mil na conta desse golpista, e o José transferiu o carro para a pessoa que comprou. Então, ambos caíram num golpe”, explicou Bianca.

José gravou um vídeo garantindo que os compradores do carro não tinham envolvimento com o crime, pois pagaram pelo veículo. O conteúdo foi encontrado no computador dele, que estava desbloqueado.

José Luis da Costa Oliveira, de 25 anos, saiu com outra roupa minutos após chegar em apartamento em SP — Foto: Reprodução

Além do vídeo, a família teve acesso aos registros de viagens feitas por José por meio de aplicativos. Os dados ajudaram a reconstituir o trajeto percorrido pelo jovem. Confira a linha do tempo:

Viagem via aplicativo: José solicitou uma corrida via aplicativo momentos após transferir o carro para a compradora, no dia 8 de outubro. O motorista da corrida revelou que o jovem estava chorando no trajeto e propôs pagar R$ 700 para ser levado até Santos em uma viagem particular.

Passagem pelo apartamento: O motorista aceitou a proposta. Antes de viajar, porém, José passou pelo apartamento dele, no bairro Bela Vista, em São Paulo. Câmeras registraram que ele permaneceu no imóvel por cerca de oito minutos e saiu com outra roupa;

Parada em um bar: O motorista deixou José em um bar no bairro Boqueirão, em Santos. Imagens de monitoramento registraram o jovem sozinho no estabelecimento;

Corrida de R$ 500 até Guarujá: José solicitou uma viagem por aplicativo até a balsa. Após entrar no veículo, ofereceu R$ 500 ao motorista para levá-lo a Guarujá por fora da plataforma;

Relato de tristeza: Segundo as advogadas, o motorista contou que José estava embriagado e triste por ter caído no golpe. Durante o trajeto, o jovem afirmou que queria tomar um banho de mar;

Último paradeiro conhecido: O motorista deixou José em frente a um condomínio em Guarujá. A família tentou obter imagens das câmeras do local, mas as gravações já não estavam disponíveis;

Mensagem à ex-namorada: Na noite do desaparecimento, José enviou uma mensagem a uma ex-namorada perguntando se ela estava noiva. Ela respondeu que sim e José disse que ela não o veria mais. Depois disso, a mulher não conseguiu mais contato com ele.

articles.title: 5 healthcare fights Democrats could take on after midterms sweep
articles.summary: Democrats will have leverage to try to restore the expired Obamacare tax credits, reverse Medicaid cuts and push for changes they say would make healthcare more affordable.
articles.body: Democrats’ victories in the midterm elections could have a major impact on Americans’ healthcare, from how much people pay for health insurance and prescription drugs to what coverage is available to them, according to health policy experts and former White House advisers. If the Democrats and President Donald Trump are willing to work together, that is. With control of the House and Senate, Democrats will hold significant leverage to restore the enhanced Affordable Care Act subsidies, reverse cuts to Medicaid and push for changes they say would make healthcare more affordable. They can also use their oversight powers to scrutinize the Trump administration’s health policies, including those led by Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. The new Democratic majority will include three doctors who have been vocal in their criticism of the health secretary, including Sen.-elect Annie Andrews of South Carolina, Sen.-elect Abdul El-Sayed of Michigan, and Rep.-elect Richard Pan of California. During her campaign, Andrews criticized Kennedy for overhauling the federal vaccine schedule and promoting medical disinformation, calling him an “archnemesis” to public health. “We’ve seen a real transformation of the healthcare state over the last two years and it’s been immensely damaging,” said Miranda Yaver, an assistant professor of health policy and management at the University of Pittsburgh. “We can absolutely expect to see a lot of oversight into these changes and unpacking what those harms are.” But turning those policies into law won’t be easy. Any legislation would still need Trump’s signature, setting up a potential clash over the future of healthcare. Ahead of Tuesday’s election, Trump said he’d brand himself “Mr. Veto” if Democrats took control of Congress. On Wednesday, he said he’ll “probably” get along with the Democrats. “The way I think about this is hunting versus farming,” said John Barkett, a former White House policy adviser under the Biden administration, where he covered drug pricing. “Next Congress, there’s going to be a lot of farming. Hunting, you go for a big kill. If those pass, probably not going to happen [with Trump]. But can you sow seeds and prepare land for growth over time? Yes.” Here are five ways Democrats could take on healthcare. ACA subsidies House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries has said restoring the expired enhanced ACA tax credits would be a primary objective for Democrats if they took control of Congress in 2027. When those federal subsidies expired at the end of last year, millions saw their monthly premium bills double or even triple — forcing about 3 million people to walk away from their coverage altogether. Others switched to cheaper plans that offered worse coverage. In 2027, costs are expected to rise even more. ACA premiums are jumping by double digits for the second year in a row, and a mix of lower enrollment and rising healthcare costs is driving some major insurers to pull out of the market. Larry Levitt, executive vice president for health policy at KFF, a nonpartisan health policy research group, said that if Democrats manage to negotiate a deal with Trump to restore the enhanced subsidies, the relief could be backdated to the beginning of 2027. That means anyone who paid the higher premiums would get that money back as a refund. “That could both increase enrollment and provide cost relief to current ACA enrollees,” he said. Dr. Ezekiel Emanuel, a special adviser for health policy during the Obama administration, said he supports Democrats pursuing reimplementing ACA subsidies as long as they can find the money for it and they don’t lose sight of rising insurance costs for other Americans. “One of the dangers of big election victories is people get cocky and they overreach and they fail to deliver on what people actually care about,” he said. “Half of all Americans get their insurance through employer-sponsored insurance.” Medicaid cuts The Medicaid cuts under Trump’s “big, beautiful bill,” especially the Medicaid work requirements, are also expected to draw significant pushback from Democrats. The work requirements are expected to strip coverage from millions of people — not for lack of employment, but due to burdensome paperwork and other red tape. A number of states have already started implementing the requirements ahead of the national Jan. 1 deadline. Last week, a federal judge in Boston dealt a blow to the administration’s work rules, blocking a policy from the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services that would have forced “medically frail” patients and people with disabilities to prove they are too “significantly impaired” to adhere to the new work mandates. The judge also granted states an additional six months to implement the more lenient version. Levitt said Trump is bound to veto any bills rolling back Medicaid cuts. “Then the game of chess between Democrats and Trump will begin to figure out what healthcare can actually get enacted,” Levitt said. It’s also possible a number of states could finally expand Medicaid. Ten states have not adopted the full Medicaid expansion under the ACA. That includes Georgia, Texas and Wisconsin, which elected Democratic governors on Tuesday, alongside Kansas, where the race remains too close to call. Yaver was skeptical, noting that Trump’s “big, beautiful bill” ended financial incentives that encouraged states to adopt the expansion. “I think we’re absolutely going to see efforts to increase Medicaid access,” she said. “I just don’t know what Medicaid expansion looks like without the increased financial incentive.” Affordability and corporate greed Democrats could find common ground with Trump on efforts to lower healthcare costs, particularly prescription drug prices, Emanuel said. Trump has made lowering drug costs a priority during his second term, through his discount prescription drug website TrumpRx and his “most favored nation” drug pricing deals. Democrats could push to build on those efforts, while pursuing other changes they say would make drugs more affordable. “I think there is probably a very big agreement you could reach with him,” Emanuel said. But Democrats may not find the dealmaker they want in Trump, Barkett said. “Remember, the big thing Trump has done on drug prices is sign these deals that no one has seen with drug manufacturers, and it’s not even clear the drug manufacturers were hurt by those deals,” Barkett said. Yaver said another way Democrats could work with Trump is through legislation limiting the use of prior authorization, a cost-cutting tool insurers use that requires patients to get approval before receiving certain treatments. The tool has been blamed by doctors and patients for delaying necessary care. The Trump administration has already made moves to crack down on the practice. “That is generating not just bipartisan support but unanimous support at the state level,” she said. There could also be a bipartisan pushback on the rising cost of hospital care as well as pharmacy benefit managers, which act as middlemen to negotiate drug prices and rebates on behalf of insurers and employers. The PBMs have faced criticisms after research has shown their practices can drive up the cost of healthcare. Investigations into the administration With control of congressional committees, Democrats will have power to hold hearings, demand documents and subpoena administration officials to testify. Emanuel said Kennedy is likely to face Democratic probes over his moves on vaccines, including overhauling the CDC’s vaccine advisory panel, changing the federal vaccine schedule and taking steps to alter the federal Vaccine Injury Compensation Program. The health secretary has also faced widespread criticism and blame for the resurgence of measles in the U.S. This year, there have been more than 4,850 measles cases, the highest number in at least 30 years. “Some of that does need to happen because that has to stop,” Emanuel said. Barkett said the investigations might play to the Democrats’ advantage by distracting the Trump administration and potentially freezing any new policies. “It takes up their time,” he said. “And everything they encounter, whatever they uncover, could be more campaign fodder [for 2028].” ‘Medicare for All’ “Medicare for All” will remain a central goal for many Democrats, even if the proposal is unlikely to become law under a Republican president. The most popular version of the proposal would establish a government-run health insurance program covering all Americans. “I’m not a big advocate of ‘Medicare for All,’ but at the moment, the only plan out there is ‘Medicare for All,’” Emanuel said. “We need to have more plans, and we have between now and the start of 2028 to have plans.” Still, introducing a “Medicare for All” bill and pushing for a vote could give supporters a chance to make their case and build momentum for a broader overhaul of the healthcare system if Democrats win the White House in 2028. That falls under “the more symbolic category, because as we know, Donald Trump is going to veto big progressive actions,” Yaver said.

articles.body: PUNE: PM Narendra Modi Wednesday requested NCP-SP chief Sharad Pawar, 85, who was discharged from a private hospital, to focus on his health, saying his daughter and Baramati MP Supriya Sule would take care of the country along with him.“PM Modi called up Pawar saheb this morning to enquire about his health. He spoke with great warmth and respect and suggested that Pawar saheb should take complete rest,” Vitthal Maniyar, a close associate of Sharad Pawar, told the media.Maniyar said Modi urged Pawar not to worry about work and to focus on his recovery.“PM told Pawar saheb that Supriya is ready and that he, along with Supriya, will look after the country, while Pawar saheb should focus on his health,” Maniyar said.Pawar thanked the PM for enquiring about his health and assured him that he would take rest. Pawar was admitted to Ruby Hall Clinic in Pune on Monday morning after complaining of pleuritic pain.After undergoing treatment for two days, he was discharged on Wednesday.In a statement, Dr Purvez K Grant, managing trustee of Ruby Hall Clinic, said, “He is stable and doing well. articles.title: Midwives' union warns over maternity unit plans in Norfolk
articles.summary: The RCM union says possible closures in Norfolk would also affect patients in neighbouring counties.
articles.body:
The Royal College of Midwives (RCM) said it was concerned by reports that two maternity units could close.

Norfolk has maternity units at hospitals in Norwich, Gorleston and King's Lynn, with the latter two also serving Cambridgeshire and Suffolk.

The trade union posted on Facebook that local maternity services should be invested in rather than cut.

The Norfolk and Waveney University Hospitals Group (NWUHG) has set out its "Case for Change" on how services could be delivered in future, but stressed that no decisions had been made and no consultation had begun. NHS leaders said any move to concentrate services at one or two sites would be based on providing safer care for women and babies.

However, the RCM warned that closing units serving rural and isolated communities could mean women travelling "unacceptable distances" while in labour.

If maternity services were removed from hospitals, the union said neonatal units and children's inpatient wards would also close because the services were inter-dependent.

Options include keeping services as they are, or closing consultant-led maternity units at the James Paget Hospital in Gorleston, the Queen Elizabeth Hospital in King's Lynn, or both.

As well as women in Norfolk, the plans could affect women in Lowestoft and north Suffolk who give birth in Gorleston and those in Wisbech and north-east Cambridgeshire who travel to King's Lynn.

The RCM argued the proposals risked worsening existing inequalities in maternity outcomes and said the answer was investment and more staffing, rather than allowing services to "shrink".

It also said closures could result in midwives being redeployed further from home.

The Facebook post said: "Women and babies deserve safe, local care, and closing units is not the answer."

The Department of Health and Social Care has been contacted for comment.

New hospitals must offer emergency care, NHS told

Two hospitals at risk of losing maternity units

NWUHG said 60 clinicians had helped develop the review.

The Case for Change argues that falling birth rates, workforce shortages and increasing numbers of women requiring more complex care are making it harder to sustain specialist services at every site.

Lesley Dwyer, NWUHG chief executive and a former midwife, previously told the BBC the review was one of the most significant pieces of work undertaken by the organisation and was aimed at making services sustainable in the long term.

"The scenarios examined so far are a starting point for further assessment, not formal proposals," she said.

"No preferred approach has been identified and no decision has been made to close or relocate these services.

"Patient safety must remain at the centre of this work. We also need to understand what different approaches could mean for choice, travel, access and the experiences of women, babies, children and families."

The work comes after NHS bosses said that smaller maternity units across the country may have to close.

The Case for Change will now be submitted to NHS England before further research and any public consultation takes place.

articles.title: College students discover new muscle attachment that could improve hip surgery
articles.summary: Two Tulane University sophomores found a previously unknown muscle in the hip during a cadaver lab session that even their professor couldn't identify.
articles.body: Two undergraduate students at Tulane University in New Orleans discovered an anatomical feature that even their professor couldn’t initially identify. Dominic Roy and Cooper Bruce were both 19-year-old college sophomores at the time of the finding in 2024. In an interview with Fox News Digital, Roy said it had been an ordinary day volunteering in the cadaver lab with R. Shane Tubbs, Ph.D., professor of neurosurgery and director of surgical anatomy at Tulane School of Medicine. 5 HABITS THAT COULD HELP KEEP YOU OUT OF A NURSING HOME, FROM AN ORTHOPEDIC SURGEON The students were dissecting several specimens’ hips to compare where the iliacus joins the psoas major, a muscle that runs from the lower back through the pelvis to the upper thigh. When looking for a particular muscle, the iliocapsularis, which sits laterally in the hip, Roy found something else instead. "I spotted a similar looking muscle that was on the other side of the Iliac fascia, close to the inguinal region of the pelvis," he said. WEEKLY WEIGHTLIFTING SWEET SPOT MAY BE LINKED TO LONGER LIFE, STUDY FINDS "I called Dr. Tubbs over and asked, ‘What is this?’ We didn't talk about this in our morning meetings ... and I think he was as stumped as me." After searching through extensive literature and textbooks to see if the muscle had been previously identified, the team came up short, which suggested it was a new discovery. "It was kind of like a reserved excitement," Bruce reflected. "Especially if the great R. Shane Tubbs can't put his finger on exactly what it is." Physicians from overseas and rising medical school students also assisted with the discovery. SIMPLE EXERCISE DONE JUST ONCE A WEEK COULD HELP LOWER BLOOD PRESSURE "Everyone kind of huddled around the same specimen and we started draping and doing the pictures … I was in awe," Roy said. "I was like, ‘Oh, wow, this is happening so quick.’ It was seriously something special." The findings were recently published in the journal Clinical Anatomy. Tubbs, who is also a co-editor-in-chief of the human anatomy reference textbook Gray's Anatomy, said Roy and Bruce’s discovery was "serendipity." "[They] identified a different part of a muscle that we had not looked at yet," he confirmed to Fox News Digital. "It's deep in the pelvis and runs out to the front of your hip." KNEE TREATMENT WITHOUT SURGERY OFFERS LASTING PAIN RELIEF FOR 80% OF ARTHRITIS PATIENTS, STUDY FINDS Potential medical uses Although the team has not yet determined the muscle’s function, clues suggest it may help stabilize the psoas major, a large muscle involved in bending the hip. The next step is to determine whether MRI scans can reveal the muscle attachment, allowing researchers to study whether its presence is linked to more or fewer symptoms, according to the doctor. "More research is needed for us to better elucidate what it does," Tubbs said. "Can you see it on imaging? Does it contribute to patients' problems? But I think this is the first step in identifying something." As minimally invasive procedures become more common, Tubbs said awareness of this small muscle could improve care, particularly for patients undergoing hip surgery. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP "They might use physical therapy to help rehab the muscle, because we did find that the fibers of this attachment directly attach into the front of the hip joint," he added. "So it may be that the muscle’s weak and causes symptoms, so you could rehab it." Doctors could also use injections to weaken the new muscle if overactivity causes pain or other symptoms. "Surgeons are replacing hips and doing hip surgery on a daily basis, so if they see the muscle, potentially they could correlate the symptoms of the patient and whether or not maybe cutting the muscle would help the patient," Tubbs said. Variations in anatomy This muscle was not found in every cadaver, the researchers noted, as each human body is different. "When you look beneath the layers of the skin, human beings have lots of variation," Tubbs said. "I tell our students that no two of you are built the same inside or out." CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR HEALTH NEWSLETTER The researchers found the same muscle attachment in gorillas, suggesting a possible evolutionary link. Bruce said this raises the question of why this muscle would still be present in some humans and not others. "Just by the nature of working with cadavers and not knowing a deep personal history of each individual … maybe this individual played soccer, or this person did a lot of rock climbing," he said. "They might've had more need for this attachment ... It's difficult to make that connection." Lessons beyond textbooks Working with real cadavers has made a big difference in shaping future doctors, Tubbs shared, as the synthetic models that are now circulating in university labs are cookie-cutter. CLICK HERE FOR MORE HEALTH STORIES "Many people have the notion ... that the entire form of the human has been worked out, and we know all the different parts. And they think we've known that for hundreds of years," he said. "But in actuality, people are still discovering things about human anatomy." Medical students "need to experience that variation" and have the hands-on experience before dealing with real patients, Roy commented. Although the new muscle attachment will have to be studied across geographic regions, Tubbs said he expects the students' discovery will eventually be added to anatomical textbooks. TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ The discovery inspired the students, now seniors, to further explore a career in medicine. Roy said he plans to enter a master’s program in anatomy. "The bottom line is that anatomical discovery doesn't end when a textbook is published ... and discovery in the anatomical sciences continues on, even in the year 2026."

articles.title: Security ⁠officer killed in stabbing attack in Jordan’s capital
articles.summary: Assailant stabbed a corporal outside the Sri Lankan embassy in Amman, killing him and injuring another officer.
articles.body:
A Jordanian security officer has been killed and another wounded in a stabbing attack outside the Sri Lankan embassy in the capital, Amman.

Jordan’s Public Security Directorate (PSD) named the officer killed in Thursday’s attack as Corporal Jawad Ali Khalaf al-Salaita, a member of the diplomatic security unit assigned to guard the embassy.

In a statement, PSD spokesperson Colonel Amer al-Sartawi said a man surprised and stabbed the victim with a sharp object on Medina al-Munawwara Street at 12:20pm (09:20 GMT). A patrol then intervened. Al-Salaita was taken to hospital but died of his wounds.

Authorities have described the attack as a “cowardly terrorist act”.

Jordan’s state-run Al-Mamlaka TV reported that the assailant attempted to seize the weapon of the security officer who was killed. A second security officer intervened to stop him, and both the assailant and the second security officer sustained injuries, it added.

Security forces cordoned off a wide area around Medina al-Munawwara Street, a busy main road in west Amman. Al Jazeera’s Tamer al-Samadi said the attack was carried out in full view of passers-by.

Security sources told Al Jazeera that the attacker, born in 1994, stabbed al-Salaita in the neck while he was inside a guard booth protecting the embassy in the Sweifieh area. According to the sources, the attacker was carrying a dagger and a knife. A second lieutenant fought him, wounded him and took control of him before he could seize the gun, but was injured in the face during the struggle.

Jordan’s PSD said a preliminary investigation indicated the attacker had been “planning to commit the terrorist act against the officers of the General Security Directorate”.

The wounded officer, born in 1988, was taken to Medical City Hospital. The PSD described his condition as stable. The attacker was taken to Dar Al Salam Hospital in critical condition.

Reporting from Aqaba, Al Jazeera’s al-Samadi said the attacker had a bag full of bladed weapons, according to preliminary investigations. Police, “counterterrorism units” and bomb disposal teams were sent to the scene.

“The information we have obtained clearly indicates that the perpetrator has terrorism records, as classified by the military State Security Court,” al-Samadi said. He reported that court files he had seen showed the attacker had been convicted years ago of joining what Jordanian authorities call “terrorist groups” and of conspiring to carry out “terrorist” acts in Jordan, and had served years in prison.

Jordan’s public prosecutor said in a statement that the State Security Court had opened an investigation into the attack.

Jordan’s minister of government communication said an attack on security personnel was “an attack on the prestige of the state and the rule of law, and an attack on every Jordanian”. He added that the government “will not tolerate any aggressor”.

The minister said the prime minister had urged officials to quickly uncover the circumstances and motives behind the attack.

State news agency Petra reported that King Abdullah II was personally following the investigation. The king and the crown prince are both abroad on official visits. Prince Faisal, acting as regent, was due to visit the wounded officer in hospital.

The attack comes weeks after gunmen opened fire during a funeral at a church in southern Jordan , killing nine people and wounding dozens more. The government also described that attack, in the city of Karak, as “terrorist”.

It was not immediately clear if the stabbing was related to the church attack.

King Abdullah said on Monday that “terrorists” would not be allowed to threaten the country’s unity and security, after the deadly church attack prompted Jordanian strikes in Syria.

articles.title: Exposure to This 1 Thing at Night May Damage Your Heart, Research Shows
articles.summary: Preventing heart disease may also depend on avoiding exposure to light during sleep, doctors say. Why sleeping in darkness is important for heart health.
articles.body: You might think you’re doing everything right to prevent heart disease — eating a healthy diet, exercising and managing blood pressure — and still miss an important risk factor. It happens during sleep, but there are simple ways to fix the problem. The key is to take a good look at your bedroom. Heart Health Tip of the Day: Avoid Exposure to Light During Sleep Nighttime light exposure while people are slumbering is linked to “adverse cardiac remodeling,” or changes to the shape and function of the heart that are typically seen with chronic stress or injury, researchers told the European Society of Cardiology. “It’s our body’s way of adapting to that stress, but ultimately it weakens the heart and can lead to heart failure,” Dr. Lu Qi, a professor at Tulane University’s School of Public Health and Tropical Medicine, said in a statement. He’s the co-author of a recent study on the subject. “Light pollution has emerged as a new risk factor for cardiovascular disease,” he added. The link between light at night and cardiovascular disease has long been overlooked, doctors previously told the National Heart, Lung and Blood Institute. Why It Matters High exposure to nighttime light was linked with a “functional decline” of the heart, specifically, the thickening of the wall of the left ventricle, which reduced the space inside that chamber, Qi and his colleagues reported in a study published in the European Heart Journal. The heart muscle’s ability to flex during a heartbeat appeared to be reduced, which is an “early indicator of heart dysfunction,” the European Society of Cardiology noted. The right ventricles and left atria of the heart also showed changes. The findings are based on data from more than 11,000 people who wore a wrist sensor for seven nights to see how much light they were typically exposed to during sleep and then underwent a cardiac MRI three years later. Artificial light at night is a “biologically active environmental stressor” that suppresses melatonin, disrupts sleep cycles, alters metabolic and inflammatory rhythms, and “ultimately affects nearly every cardiovascular cell type,” researchers wrote in an accompanying editorial. “The light in our bedrooms deserves consideration as a cardiovascular risk factor, alongside smoking, hypertension, and physical inactivity,” they warned. “Darkness deserves recognition as a vital sign, as essential to cardiovascular health as blood pressure control and clean air.” How to Get Started Make sure you sleep in the dark to protect your heart. Close the blinds and turn off all lights and light-emitting electronics. If there’s still light coming in, consider equipping the bedroom with blackout curtains or wearing an eye mask. This may be especially important if you work a night shift and must sleep during the day. “Reduction of nighttime light exposure should be considered as one of the potential strategies for preventing heart disease,” Qi said. TODAY’s Expert Tip of the Day series is all about simple strategies to make life a little easier. Every Monday through Friday, different qualified experts share their best advice on diet, fitness, heart health, mental wellness and more.

articles.title: Four people, including a child, killed in Israeli attacks on Gaza
articles.summary: Gaza officials say more than 1,600 Palestinians have been killed since the so-called ‘ceasefire’ took effect.
articles.body:
Israeli attacks have killed at least four Palestinians, including a child, in central and southern Gaza, medical sources say, as Israeli forces keep up near-daily strikes in the enclave.

Medical sources at Al-Aqsa Martyrs Hospital in Deir el-Balah said Abdul Rahim Walid Matar, 27, was killed at dawn on Thursday when an Israeli drone fired two missiles at a tent sheltering displaced people west of az-Zawayda.

Nasser Medical Complex said a woman was killed and two people were wounded by Israeli fire outside areas under Israeli military control in Khan Younis. A source at al-Awda Hospital said a child was killed by Israeli fire in Bureij refugee camp.

Reporting from Deir el-Balah, Al Jazeera’s Ashraf Amra said Israeli forces opened direct fire on homes and tents in eastern Bureij, killing the child on the spot.

“Israeli forces on the edges of the area that directly overlooks al-Mawasi are firing heavily towards the tents of displaced people,” Amra said. He added that a man sitting inside his tent was critically wounded and taken into surgery at Nasser.

Another drone strike at Az-zawaya killed another person, medical sources told Al Jazeera, bringing the death toll to four.

An Israeli drone also struck a gathering of residents in the al-Baraka area of Deir el-Balah, wounding several people, one critically.

In the north, a source at al-Shifa Hospital told Al Jazeera a Palestinian was wounded when a drone struck an apartment in al-Karama, northwest of Gaza City. Israeli artillery shelled eastern Gaza City heavily, and naval vessels fired towards the coastline.

Local sources said Israeli military vehicles fired heavily around the Hosni al-Musaddar Mosque east of Maghazi camp, and a drone dropped a bomb nearby. No injuries were reported there. Residents east of Khan Younis reported two powerful explosions as the army blew up homes and civilian facilities inside areas it controls.

Amra said Israeli forces were also pushing forward on the eastern edges of al-Musaddar and Deir el-Balah, bulldozing homes and farmland and absorbing more land behind the so-called “Yellow Line”.

On Wednesday, Gaza’s Health Ministry reported three Palestinians had been killed and 21 wounded in the previous 24 hours. One of the three had died of earlier wounds.

The ministry says 1,602 Palestinians have been killed and 5,794 wounded since the ceasefire took effect on October 11, 2025. These deaths put the overall toll since October 2023 at 74,618 killed and 175,920 wounded.

Gaza’s Government Media Office said on Monday that Israel had committed 5,989 ceasefire violations since the truce began . Of those, 753 came in October; among them 346 shootings, 310 bombardments and 64 home demolitions.

images.caption: Palestinians carry the body of Abdelrahim Matar, who was killed in an Israeli air strike, during his funeral at Al-Aqsa Hospital in Deir el-Balah, the Gaza Strip [Abdel Kareem Hana/AP]

articles.title: Southport and Nottingham attack victims call out NHS snooping
articles.summary: Families described the unauthorised access of confidential medical records as an "abuse of power".
articles.body:
Families affected by the Southport and Nottingham attacks have called for stronger safeguards against NHS staff improperly accessing confidential patient records.

In an open letter, they described the breaches as a "flagrant abuse of power" and urged ministers and NHS leaders to take further action.

More than 30 people have signed the letter, including those affected by the maternity scandals.

The BBC has contacted NHS England, the Department for Health and Social Care and Department for Culture for comment.

Grace O'Malley-Kumar, Barnaby Webber, both 19, and grandfather Ian Coates, 65, were stabbed to death in the street by Valdo Calocane in Nottingham in 2023.

The authors of the letter highlighted how, in the wake of the attack, "staff began prying, while parents were still coming to terms with the deaths of their children. Other victims were still in hospital fighting for their lives when their records were breached".

NHS workers also snooped on the records of victims of the Southport attack, when Axel Rudakubana killed Bebe King, six, Elsie Dot Stancombe, seven, and nine-year-old Alice Da Silva Aguiar during a Taylor Swift-themed dance class in 2024.

"Strangers, who had no direct involvement in their care, probed their most sensitive and personal information in a flagrant abuse of power," the authors wrote.

This "deeply troubling" behaviour has been repeated following other high profile incidents, they said.

Liverpool Heart and Chest NHS Foundation Trust is investigating allegations staff inappropriately accessed Southport stabbing victims' medical records.

In May, the University Hospitals of Liverpool Group (UHLG) admitted that nearly 50 of its staff had wrongly looked at victims' medical files and there is a separate investigation being held at North West Ambulance Service Trust in relation to staff looking up the victims of the attack without authorisation.

The authors said the issue was "not exclusive to the NHS" as they highlighted how the Ministry of Justice and HM Courts and Tribunals Service "have both apologised for inappropriate access of sensitive, personal information belonging to the Southport victims".

In September NHS officials announced a crackdown on staff inappropriately accessing patient medical records.

Health chiefs said that staff suspected of snooping will be suspended immediately and have their access to health service computer systems cut off.

But the measures do not go far enough to prevent such behaviour in the future, according to the letter.

The authors have called for a "tick box" to enable staff to access records which confirms they have legitimate reason to do so.

They have also called for audits on snooping and for patients to be "properly recognised" by the Information Commissioner.

"These breaches are deeply distressing and entirely preventable," the authors said.

"We believe these three measures would make significant progress in tackling the problem and preventing further harm."

Nicola Ryan-Donnelly, partner at Fletchers Solicitors which penned the letter, said: "We have written and published this open letter because victims of NHS snooping have had enough.

"Every week in the media we are learning of a new breach into patient's medical records by staff who have no legitimate cause to access them.

"Among the child Southport survivors I represent, many of their parents do not feel they have a voice to speak out about how this has affected them.

"They had hoped that their anonymity would protect their children's most vulnerable and difficult moments, but the truth is staff have repeatedly abused their position to pry into their most private and sensitive information.

"Anybody, no matter who they are or what they have been through, should feel confident and that staff will protect their privacy and dignity while they are being treated or cared for by the NHS and other agencies.

"Stronger sanctions and dismissals for NHS staff who snoop is a step in the right direction, but it does not do enough to address the problem.

"We have to instil a new culture in our health system and give victims a powerful voice to challenge breaches."
